Drebenstedt, C. and Singhal, R. (eds) (2014). Mine Planning and Equipment Selection: Proceedings of the 22nd MPES Conference, Dresden, Germany, 14th-19th October 2013. Springer International Publishing, Cham. ISBN 978-3-319-02677-0 (print), 978-3-319-02678-7 (eBook). DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-02678-7. Papers used: Paraszczak, J., Fytas, K. and Laflamme, M., Feasibility of Using Electric Trucks in Deep Metal Mines, pp.1265-1275; Curi, A., Felsch, W.S., Rodovalho, E.C. and Meireles, B.P., Evaluation of Haul Trucks Performance in a CSN Mine, pp.1143-1150 (DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-02678-7_111); Cardu, M. and Mucci, A., Rock Excavation by Drilling and Blasting: Evaluation of the Performance of the Equipment in an Open Pit Limestone Quarry, pp.1127-1142 (DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-02678-7_110); Mafuta, R.K., Fytas, K., Paraszczak, J. and Laflamme, M., Impact of Diesel Equipment on Ventilation in Quebec Underground Mines, pp.571-579 (DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-02678-7_55); Apel, D., Liu, W. and Bindiganavile, V., Simulation of the Effects of Thermo Insulating Shotcrete on the Energy Consumption of Ventilation and Cooling Systems at Deep Underground Mines, pp.37-42.

Locators are printed page numbers of the proceedings; PDF page offsets drift (front matter about +24, p.571 about -5, p.1143 about -38, p.1265 about -43). Targeted pass over a 1464-page, 2-volume Springer proceedings: table of contents plus full-text keyword search (electric, battery, trolley, LHD, haul truck, fuel consumption, kWh/t, ventilation, comminution, conveyor). Papers USED: (1) Paraszczak, Fytas, Laflamme, Feasibility of Using Electric Trucks in Deep Metal Mines, p.1265-1275: battery truck specs (Table 1), Kiruna/Atlas Copco EMT-35/EMT-50 trolley truck specs (Table 2), trolley supply line 1400 $/m and roadbed 345 $/m (2007 Ontario estimate, CAD assumed), truck life over 10 years; relative cost, air and productivity figures in _other-values; trucking cost per t 19 % lower in _measures. (2) Curi et al., Evaluation of Haul Trucks Performance in a CSN Mine, p.1143-1150: open-pit diesel haul-truck fuel per tonne (L/t) and per hour, mechanical vs diesel-electric fleets on two routes (fleet totals loaded, per-truck rows not; truck model and payload not printed). (3) Cardu and Mucci, open-pit limestone quarry equipment, p.1127-1142: Perlini DP905/DP705 payload, power, measured 44 L/h, fleet investment per truck and catalogue EUR/t (reprinted InfoMine 2010); CAT 385C excavator 63 L/h. (4) Mafuta et al., Impact of Diesel Equipment on Ventilation in Quebec Underground Mines, p.571-579: airflow indices only, in _other-values. (5) Apel et al., thermo-insulating shotcrete, p.37-42: simulated heat-load reductions in _measures. CHECKED AND REJECTED (no technology-level energy or cost numbers): Noll and Mischo, Ventilation on Demand decision tool (p.133); Pandey, Ventilation design of long sub-surface headings (p.165); Pivnyak et al., Decrease of power consumption in fine grinding (p.1069, theoretical, no kWh/t); Kozyaruk, Growth directions of the electric drive of the mining and transport complex (p.1215, qualitative); Drebenstedt keynote (p.3, biodiesel mentioned without numbers). Fuel volumes are in litres as printed (diesel density and heating value not printed). Euro prices carry no price year: publication year 2014 used. Composed technology names: haul-truck_trolley-electric (full trolley), haul-truck_diesel-fleet_mechanical, haul-truck_diesel-fleet_rigid, haul-truck_diesel-electric, excavator_hydraulic-diesel.
